messages:
mike: quick synopsis — trying an experiment for a 'hotstart' policy on KV prefix cache during deploys. saw hit-rate drop from ~78% to ~43% after the last roll. asking ops if we can run a small seeder that backfills recent prefixes + synthetic variants at deploy time. impact: p50 latency +40ms, p99 spikes during cold bursts. :warning:
li: saw the same in canary. profiler points to cache key mismatch: tokenization/normalization changed and our prefix-keyer wasn't canonicalizing new tokens, so many keys miss.
sanjay: to confirm — kernel selection tweak changed token chunking for short sequences? that could shift KV keys if the keyer uses raw token IDs.
mike: yeah, we changed the kernel heuristics for tiny batches (optimize for latency) and it altered early tokenization offsets. not intentional.
jamie: idea: instead of a full scheduled seeder, trigger a deploy-time job that reads last 10k unique prefixes from traffic logs and pushes canonicalized keys into KV. cheaper and targeted. also attach a throttling window to avoid thundering herd. :rocket:
maya: +1 for targeted backfill. also propose a feedback loop: if live KV hit-rate drops below 60% for 5m, autoscaler hook triggers a synthetic seeding pass for top n prefixes. keep iterations small (n=1k) and exponential backoff.
alex: I'll wire a metric (redwood.kv.hit_rate) and an alert rule. plan: alert when hit_rate < 0.6 for 5m AND p50 latency increased > 20% vs baseline. add a tag for 'deploy_candidate' so we can suppress noise.
li: small config sketch for seeder (works with our submit-job API):
```yaml
job: kv-seeder
source: recent-prefixes-query
limit: 1000
throttle_rps: 50
canonicalize: true
retry_policy:
  retries: 3
  backoff_s: 30
```
jamie: ops note — prefer hook on autoscale 'scale-up' event too. when new nodes come up they announce themselves and the seeder can push only keys targeted to those nodes' shards. reduces cross-shard noise.
sanjay: performance note: seeding itself can affect kernel selection and batching heuristics (adds synthetic short requests). ensure seeder uses a separate runtime profile so it doesn't change production batching distribution. e.g. set header `x-infer-purpose: seeder`.
mike: good catch. we'll send seeder traffic to a dedicated pool or mark it low-priority. also need to avoid updating live KV schema during hot path.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-10T15:24 started by @mike for service inference-runtime-v2. :eyes:
mike: experiment plan: 1) canonicalize keyer so tokenization changes don't flip keys, 2) run a stage deploy with deploy-time seeder (limit=1k), 3) monitor hit_rate and latency for 30m, 4) enable autoscale-hook seeding if improvement observed.
alex: I'll add dashboards: 1) kv hit-rate over time (per model, per region), 2) seeder RPS & errors, 3) p50/p99 by cache-hit vs miss.
maya: one caution — synthetic seeding can hide real regressions. we should tag seeded prefixes and include seeded=false filter in our regression evals for a week after rollout.
li: we should also add a quick regression test in the canary: run 200 sample prefixes before/after kernel change to measure key stability. if >5% prefix-key flip, fail canary.
mike: agreed. last ask: ops, can we schedule a short dry-run today at 17:00 UTC with throttle 20rps and limit 500? will post results in this thread.
jamie: can do. will create job and post job-id.
deploy-bot: job created: seeder-job-1789123501 (throttle=20rps, limit=500).
mike: thanks — will follow up with numbers.
